records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Read before writing bpy geometry code that sizes, orients or joins primitives (size vs radius, Euler axis choice, rotation_mode discard, flush-vs-overlap joints, scale_length export units), then build a connection map and run a mechanical verification checklist. Not for read-only scene inspection (stated); does not authorize file export, saves or live-scene resets.
records.content_finding: High-value failure-mode skill: concrete version-pinned measurements (Blender 4.5.13 LTS), a mechanically checkable connection-map convention and a runnable verifier with tolerances. Main caveats are the destructive clear_scene in the verifier if run in a live session and the half-volume artefact in the normals check; neither is an authority hard fail.
records.bundled_file_findings: Single-file package (SKILL.md); embeds a ~200-line verify_assembly.py (bpy/mathutils only; deletes all objects in a fresh factory-startup scene, builds a 4-part example, prints JSON PASS/FAIL, non-zero exit on failure). No network, subprocess or credential reads. Static check: rotation/size claims are mathematically correct (Rx(90) maps +Z to -Y, Ry(90) to +X, aim +Y = (-90,0,0)); the signed-volume check uses only the first triangle of each polygon, so reported volumes are ~half true volume (e.g. plate 8.64e-05 vs 1.728e-04 m^3) - adequate as a sign test only.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No external communication, credentials or network. The embedded verify_assembly.py calls clear_scene() (select_all + object.delete of every object) and resets unit settings; it is explicitly framed for `blender --background --factory-startup`, where that is harmless, but there is no warning against pasting it into a live user session via execute_python, where it would delete the user's scene objects without confirmation. Scene-level only; no file writes besides what the user runs.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Use when a Blender task touches UV maps/texture coordinates via the dcc-mcp typed tool surface instead of raw blender-scripting. Not for topology/modifiers (blender-mesh), material slots or shader graphs, UV distortion/texel-density measurement, or any Blender not driven through this MCP bridge; it does not authorize file saves or remote code.
records.content_finding: A well-engineered typed tool surface with precise behavioural contracts (Object Mode requirement, success/complete/passed semantics, triangle-count caveats, no-overwrite SVG export) and honest annotation of the one destructive tool. Its value is tightly coupled to the dcc-mcp-blender server and dcc-mcp-core runtime, so it is reference material for MCP tool design rather than a portable skill; there is no per-action confirmation for delete_uv_map inside the skill itself.
records.bundled_file_findings: 12 scripts are ~400-byte shims that import dcc_mcp_core.skill.skill_entry and delegate to functions in repository-level dcc_mcp_blender._uv_ops / _uv_quality (present at pin; spot-checked delete_uv_map: mesh.uv_layers.remove after name validation; export_uv_layout: absolute .svg path, refuses existing output, exclusive-create write). tools.yaml (13 KB) defines strict JSON input schemas (additionalProperties:false, enums, bounded budgets such as max_triangles<=500000, max_pair_tests<=2000000) and read_only/destructive/idempotent annotations per tool. Minor docstring copy-paste: export_uv_layout.py docstring says 'Read source UV data without changing Blender context' though it writes a file.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Consequential actions are in-scene mutations of the user's open Blender session (create/copy/delete UV maps, project/unwrap/pack/normalize) plus one local file write (export_uv_layout writes a new absolute .svg; implementation checks path.exists() and opens with mode 'x', refusing overwrite). delete_uv_map removes a UV layer without an in-skill confirmation but is annotated destructive_hint=true in tools.yaml so an MCP host can gate it; this is a scene edit within the requested domain, not a destructive file/repo operation, and no file save of the .blend occurs. No network calls, no subprocess, no credential reads, no arbitrary Python exec in these tools; open_world_hint=true on export only reflects the filesystem write. No personal data flows.
records.capability_specific: Typed Blender UV unwrap, projection, packing, audit and SVG export tools

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 2/2: description names UV maps/texture coordinates and explicit routing ('use before falling back to blender-scripting'; prefer blender-mesh/materials/shader-nodes for other work).
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 2/2: states mode preconditions, selection behaviour, layer reacquisition, audit scopes (per_object vs selection), allow_stacked, udim semantics and export layout modes.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 1/2: mutations are in-scene and requested-domain; delete_uv_map flagged destructive_hint but no in-skill confirmation step; export refuses overwrite; no exec/network.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 2/2: missing layer/failed operator returns error with conservative mutation receipt; packing skips normalization on failure; budget exhaustion yields complete=false/passed=false; callers told to inspect success.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 2/2: requires both context.complete and context.passed for a clean audit, warns disabling overlap is not acceptance, discloses that distortion/texel density are not measured and export is not a quality pass.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 2/2: every script's delegated module (_uv_ops.py, _uv_quality.py) exists at the pin and tools.yaml source_file entries match the scripts present.
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: preconditions declare Blender>=4.0 and open scene, but the hard dependency on the dcc-mcp server and dcc-mcp-core version pin is only implicit via imports.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 2/2: specific UV-quality audit (degenerate/tile/overlap with budgets) and SVG layout export are differentiated beyond generic bpy scripting.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 1/2: strict schemas and name validation bound inputs, but object names/paths are caller-supplied with no guidance on untrusted scene content; no embedded agent instructions found.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 2/2: typed, bounded, idempotency-annotated tools with machine-readable receipts are well designed for agent use.

records.salvage: Tool-annotation pattern (read_only/destructive/idempotent/open_world hints per tool), complete+passed two-flag audit semantics with shared budgets, and exclusive-create no-overwrite file export.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Use before export/publish in a dcc-mcp-driven Blender session to get severity-coded, stable-issue-code validation reports. Not for repairing issues, image decoding or render validation, or Blender sessions outside this MCP bridge; it does not authorize export or publishing.
records.content_finding: Safe, read-only validation surface with structured severity reports, but SKILL.md is a 4-sentence stub: it does not list check names, rule keys, supported target formats or issue codes, so an agent must discover them by trial or by reading repository source. Useful as reference for machine-readable validation report design; procedural value from the skill text alone is thin.
records.bundled_file_findings: 6 scripts are ~400-byte shims delegating to dcc_mcp_blender._asset_pipeline_ops (present at pin; report construction and storage checked). tools.yaml (6.3 KB) defines input schemas; validate_materials documents resource_checks_complete and limits clearly, but checks/rules objects for run_scene_checks, validate_mesh, validate_animation and validate_export_readiness are open (additionalProperties:true, unenumerated check names and target_format) with no documentation of allowed values.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: All six tools are annotated read_only=true/destructive=false. Implementation stores reports only in an in-process dict (_REPORTS, _LATEST_REPORT_ID) in _asset_pipeline_ops.py; validate_materials docstring states it never loads, reloads or writes images. File-writing functions in the same module (create_publish_manifest, prepare_publish_package) are not exposed by this package. No network, subprocess, credential or personal-data flows. No consequential action, so no gate required.
